props.gloss_en: the mishna: boats tied together -- one may carry from one to the other
Rava: [the mishna] was needed only to permit the small boat between them
Rav Safra: [the mishna] was needed only [to teach] making an eruv and carrying from one to the other
boats tied to each other -- one makes an eruv and carries from one to the other
if [the ties] were severed -- they are forbidden
if they were tied again -- whether unwittingly, intentionally, under duress or by mistake -- they return to their former permission
and so mats spread toward the public domain -- one makes an eruv and carries from one to the other
if they were rolled up -- forbidden
if spread again -- whether unwittingly, intentionally, under duress or by mistake -- they return to their former permission
for any partition made on Shabbat, whether unwittingly or intentionally, is [called] a partition
Rav Nachman: they taught [that a partition made on Shabbat is a partition] only for throwing, but to carry is forbidden
when Rav Nachman's [dictum] was stated, it was stated of an intentional [act]
Shmuel: even if [the boats] are tied with the string of a cloak
actually, [Shmuel speaks of a string] that can hold them
[the alternative:] Shmuel speaks of a string that cannot hold them
the mishna: if one tied [the boat] with something that holds it -- it brings impurity to it
with something that does not hold it -- it does not bring impurity to it
and Shmuel said: provided it is tied with an iron chain
for impurity it is so, as it is written 'by the slain of the sword' (Num 19:16) -- a sword is like the slain
but for Shabbat, since it can hold it, it is a mere sign -- even the string of a cloak

objections.gloss_en: אמר ליה רב ספרא: משה, שפיר קאמרת?! 'מטלטלין מזו לזו' תנן -- the mishna says one carries from one boat to the other, not via a boat between them

איני?! והאמר רב נחמן: לא שנו אלא לזרוק, אבל לטלטל אסור -- an amoraic dictum against the baraita's 'any partition made on Shabbat is a partition' (kind svara: no objection kind exists for an amoraic-memra contradiction)
